sentences.text:
The present application under Section 389 of the Cr.P.C. seeks suspension of sentence and grant of bail during the pendency of the present appeal.
2.

The present appellant/applicant has been convicted under Section 376(2)(n) of the IPC and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 10 years alongwith fine of Rs. 10,000/- and in default of payment of fine, further simple imprisonment for 2 months.
The appellant/applicant has been further convicted under Section 506 of the IPC and has been sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for 1 year.
3. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant/applicant This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 21/09/2023 at 23:03:12 submits that from reading of the evidence of victim/PW-1, it can be reasonably inferred that the relationship between the appellant/applicant and the victim were consensual in nature.

Admittedly,
the victim/PW-1 was a major at the time of the incident.

It is the case of the prosecution that she got admitted in the hospital and delivered the baby and thereafter the present FIR was registered at her instance against the present appellant/applicant.

1 4.

Learned counsel for the appellant/applicant has drawn the attention of this Court to the cross-examination of the victim/PW-1, wherein she stated at the said point of time while playing ludo she started loving the appellant/applicant.

Attention of this Court is also drawn to the statement of PW-1 under Section 164 of the Cr.PC made before the learned Metropolitan Magistrate,
whereby she did not make any allegation with regard to forceful intercourse.

It is further submitted that as per the nominal roll dated 11.09.2023, received from the Office of the Superintendent,
Central Jail No. 8/9, Tihar, New Delhi, the present appellant/applicant has already undergone half of the sentence awarded to him.

entities.text:
Office of the Superintendent,
Central Jail No. 8/9, Tihar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
It is submitted that the appeal is not likely be taken up for hearing,
therefore, the present application for suspension of sentence may be allowed.

5. Per contra learned APP for the State submits that the victim/PW-1 has categorically alleged with regard to forceful nature of relationship between them in the FIR as well as in her testimony, during her examination-in-chief.
It is further submitted that the victim in the present case as per her mother suffers from epilepsy and therefore was not in a sound state of mind.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7. The statement of the victim recorded as per the FIR clearly states This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 21/09/2023 at 23:03:12 about the forceful nature of relationship between them and the threat extended by the present applicant/appellant at the time of the incident.
The said statement of PW-1/victim before the learned Trial Court has been consistent to that effect.
The cross-examination of the witness as pointed hereinabove cannot be seen in isolation.
Testimony of the victim/PW-1 has clearly brought out the forceful nature of the relationship and the act on part of the present appellant/applicant.
Prima facie at this stage, it cannot be said that the relation between the appellant/applicant and the victim was consensual in nature.
However, it is the subject matter of hearing the present appeal.
8. In view of the facts and circumstances, the present application is dismissed and disposed of accordingly.
9. Copy of this order be sent to concerned Jail Superintendent for necessary information and compliance.

10. List for hearing on 31.10.2023 at 02:15 PM.
11.

In the meantime, the parties are at liberty to file a brief written synopsis of their submissions,
running into not more than 3 pages, alongwith the relevant judgments on which they seek to place reliance upon, after providing an advance copy to the opposite side before the next date of hearing.
AMIT SHARMA, J SEPTEMBER 19, 2023/bsr
